final_recommendation: The room converged on a comprehensive trilateral package signed end-of-business the following day, with all core provisions locked verbatim in a unified legal memo: 75% RVC with 36-month phase-in, automatic labor enforcement clawback (30-day trigger, no State waiver), Chapter 19 dispute settlement, unanimous-termination sunset clause, and 3.25/3.5% Canadian dairy access. Legal teams received formatting-only authority, eliminating discretion that threatened ratification timelines.
minority_objections: Supply-chain manufacturers repeatedly raised uncertainty about whether the six-year review would auto-renew on identical RVC/labor terms or trigger full renegotiation—this was never definitively answered in the transcript
Auto industry initially hedged on capex commitment until legal scope was locked to formatting-only
key_conflicts: Canada's Chapter 19 red line vs. U.S. pressure to finalize without it (resolved by locking Chapter 19 in unified text)
Automatic vs. discretionary clawback enforcement—labor/Congress demanded mandatory language, Canada initially pushed discretionary (resolved by automatic 30-day trigger)
Legal teams' scope of authority—multiple parties feared 'clarifying edits' would soften enforcement (resolved by written memo restricting legal to formatting/citations only)
Dairy access percentages—U.S. ag demanded written commitment before Canada would move on other issues (resolved at 3.25/3.5%)
key_concessions: Canada accepted 3.25/3.5% dairy market access in exchange for Chapter 19 preservation and unanimous sunset clause
Mexico committed to unannounced labor inspections with 48-hour notice and no pre-approval authority
U.S. accepted unanimous-termination sunset clause instead of unilateral withdrawal option
All parties accepted 36-month phase-in to 75% RVC instead of immediate compliance
red_lines: Canada: Chapter 19 dispute settlement must remain in text (stated multiple times as 'non-negotiable')
Labor/Congress: Automatic clawback with no State discretion to waive enforcement
Mexico: 48-hour notice language must prohibit pre-approval coordination
Canada: Sunset clause must require unanimous agreement to terminate, not unilateral U.S. withdrawal
Multiple parties: Legal teams restricted to formatting-only, zero substantive rewording authority
ignored_or_underweighted_risks: Six-year renewal mechanism ambiguity—whether RVC/labor terms auto-renew identically or trigger full renegotiation was raised by supply-chain and auto industry in R8-R9 but never resolved in transcript
Actual enforcement capacity in Mexico—while 48-hour notice was locked, no discussion of inspector training, funding, or institutional capacity to conduct unannounced audits
Congressional ratification timeline risk—Canada demanded Parliament vote Monday but no discussion of whether U.S. Congress could actually move that quickly
Steel/aluminum tariff interaction with auto rules—mentioned in marker definition but never surfaced in negotiation
downstream_risk_variables: Whether legal teams actually honor formatting-only constraint or find ways to 'clarify' substantive provisions
Canadian Parliament ratification vote outcome on Monday timeline
U.S. Congressional ratification floor dynamics once enforcement language becomes public
Supply-chain restructuring costs and timeline feasibility for 36-month phase-in
Mexican institutional capacity to execute unannounced inspections at scale
Year-seven renewal negotiation—whether identical terms hold or full renegotiation occurs
uncertainty_notes: The six-year review auto-renewal question (whether RVC/labor terms stay identical for years 7-12 or trigger renegotiation) was raised explicitly by supply-chain manufacturers and auto industry in R8-R9 but never answered by USTR or locked in the memo. This creates investment uncertainty for capex decisions despite the package otherwise closing. Additionally, while enforcement language was locked verbatim, no discussion occurred about Mexican government capacity to actually execute the inspection regime at scale.

marker_evidence.auto_rules_bottleneck: 75% RVC with 36-month phase-in was the core framework locked in R1-R2, drove the clawback enforcement design, and required written legal-scope memo in R8-R9 to prevent softening—shaped the entire package structure
marker_evidence.labor_enforcement_key: Automatic 30-day clawback with no State waiver was Congress's explicit ratification condition (R2-R3), drove Mexico's 48-hour notice commitment (R8), and required written legal memo (R9) to prevent 'clarifying edits'—directly tied to U.S. ratification floor votes
marker_evidence.canada_dairy_final_issue: Canada made dairy access (3.25/3.5%) contingent on Chapter 19 being locked in same package (R2), stated it 'comes off the table' if Chapter 19 fails (R2), and required unified memo (R9) to prevent separate appendix—blocking item that shaped final package
marker_evidence.dispute_settlement_canada_redline: Canada stated Chapter 19 'non-negotiable' (R5), required it locked verbatim in legal draft (R6-R7), and made it condition for dairy concession (R2)—explicit red line that drove package structure
marker_evidence.sunset_to_review_compromise: Supply-chain manufacturers stated they 'won't restructure for a deal that gets ripped up' (R3), drove USTR's six-year review with unanimous-termination proposal (R4), and required verbatim legal lock (R7-R8) to prevent 'review and renegotiate' rewording—shaped sunset clause design
marker_evidence.ratification_risk: Congress demanded automatic clawback language 'or this doesn't clear the Hill' (R2), required written legal-scope memo 'or my members don't move' (R8), and Canada required Parliament vote Monday on signed text (R8)—ratification constraints drove legal-memo mechanism and signature timeline
marker_evidence.supply_chain_adjustment: Raised compliance costs and sourcing restructuring (R1), questioned 30-day vs. phase-in timeline (R1), and asked about six-year renewal horizon (R7-R9)—acknowledged as concern but did not block or reshape core proposals
marker_evidence.us_mexico_first_pressures_canada: Mexico stated 'we're all explaining why trilateral fell apart over process' if Canada doesn't join (R1), and USTR threatened 'sign tomorrow or we move forward with Mexico alone' (R7)—raised as leverage but Canada's red lines (Chapter 19, dairy) were accommodated rather than overridden
